Abstract excerpt: Large language models increasingly serve as persistent conversational assistants, requiring memory that preserves relevant experience and maintains continuity across interactions. Existing methods improve access to conversational history through long-context processing, selective retrieval, and structured memory organization. However, most systems treat memory access as retrieving relevant past information without first determining which prior interaction state the current turn resumes.
